thread.title: Apple: 5th Best Still Great - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Bill Maurer
title: Apple: 5th Best Still Great - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Back in April, one report noted that Apple's ( AAPL ) newest product, the HomePod, was off to a very slow start . There may have been a multitude of reasons for this, like a premium price and limited initial features. A few months later, another research firm has come out with a note that appears to be quite negative for the device. However, when looking at the data in terms of the entire Apple and technology universe, investors might be quite pleased.
Just recently, Canalys published a report detailing Apple trailing competitors Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google ( GOOG ) ( GOOGL ) in the smart speaker space, with the main premise below:
Canalys expects the smart speaker installed base will approach the 100-million barrier by the end of this year, making it almost 2.5 times bigger than at the end of 2017. The installed base will keep growing, more than doubling in size to reach 225 million units by 2020. Amazon Echo devices will account for over 50% of the installed base in 2018, while Google’s Home series will account for 30%. Apple’s HomePod models will trail, accounting for a meager 4% of the 2018 base.
If you were a first timer to this arena, you would be pretty down on Apple. However, you have to remember two key points here. First, the HomePod only launched earlier this year thanks to a delay in late 2017, while Amazon and Google have had their respective devices on the market for quite some time. Second, the HomePod starts at $349, while we see Amazon and Google at much lower price points.
So just like when we compare the Apple Watch to Fitbit ( FIT ) in terms of wearables, the market share number in terms of unit sales is likely well below what the revenue share is . But even beyond that, the Canalys article doubles down on its negativity, suggesting Apple will struggle to only get to a 10% market share in 2022 by providing the following chart.
( Source: Canalys article linked above)
So let's assume that Apple gets to a 10% share by then, which based on the growth in the space above means about 31 million unit will be in use by then. Since installed base would mean currently in use, there will also be sales from devices in previous years that are no longer in use, so let's assume total HomePod sales of 40 million by then. Adding on another step, let's go with incremental growth, implying yearly sales of 2 million, then 5, 8, 11, and 14, which gets use to that 40 million total.
At 14 million unit sales by 2022, that would imply almost $4.9 billion in revenues from the HomePod that year at its current price. That's not much for Apple overall given current projections , but wouldn't any company kill to have its 5th biggest product doing $5 billion in annual revenues? This of course is ignoring the services segment, putting the HomePod behind the iPhone, Mac, iPad, and Apple Watch. Just to put this in perspective, consider the following companies that may be projected for up to or around $5 billion in revenues in 2022, based on the following estimates from Yahoo Finance.
Twitter ( TWTR ) is forecast for $3.28 billion in 2019 revenues. Snap ( SNAP ) is forecast for $1.70 billion in 2019 revenues. BlackBerry ( BB ) and Roku ( ROKU ) projected for around $925 million in 2019 revenues. iRobot ( IRBT ) is projected for $1.25 billion, Fitbit for $1.5 billion, and GoPro ( GPRO ) for $1.16 billion in 2019. Now I know that some of these companies aren't direct competitors to Apple, but by 2022, maybe only one of them will be at $5 billion in total revenues (Twitter). The Canalys note tries to put Apple in a somewhat bearish light, but we'd be talking about the company's 5th best product doing $5 billion in yearly revenues by then! Is this just another attempt by the Apple naysayers to knock the company down a notch a bit?
In the end, while the Canalys note appears to be quite bearish regarding Apple's HomePod, putting the whole thing in context actually seems quite positive. While Apple's unit share may seem low, its revenue percentage is likely much higher given the price points we are talking about. Also, having your 5th best product with a $5 billion annual revenue rate would be quite impressive, and that's not even counting the services segment that could be doing $50 billion in annual revenues by then, or other new devices like smartglasses that could be super hot. Apple remains a technology leader with several truly impressive revenue streams, and that means good things for investors in the coming years.
